Putting line numbers in the code block make it impossible to just copy and paste the code 😢.

Here's a [godbolt link](https://godbolt.org/z/8P7YrrnKz).

> Putting line numbers in the code block make it impossible to just copy and paste the code 😢.

True, but it allowed me to reference the code more easily in the bug description.

> Here's a [godbolt link](https://godbolt.org/z/8P7YrrnKz).

Nice! Didn't know Compiler Explorer supported DXC!

With some more testing, this bug not only occurs for structs of matrices, but also arrays of matrices, and any combination (array of struct of matrix, struct of array of matrix, etc.). Here's a Compiler Explorer link with a bunch of use-cases that do the wrong thing: https://godbolt.org/z/s73P9or1E

We hit this bug again, and now I realize that it happens for struct/array of (struct/array) of any type, not just of matrix. Basically it happens for const init of buffers - this includes structs, arrays, vectors, matrices, and combinations of these. I've added more test cases to show this:

https://godbolt.org/z/6MsvWrbcx

This is so broken that we're just not going to emit 'const' variables anymore in Tint until this gets fixed. I'm not sure if this will have any serious impact on performance.

title: Initializing a const-qualified var of type 'struct/array of (struct/array of) more than one type' with initializer 'init' will ignore any dynamic writes made to 'init' beforehand
